Thanks Anna — and good catch on the DST timing. Quick technical note and the fix I just applied:

Why this happens (short):
- If an event is created without an explicit IANA timezone (e.g., Europe/London) and later forwarded, some calendar clients interpret it as "floating" (no timezone anchor). When that happens, the recipient's calendar engine places it at the same nominal local time (so 11:00 in sender's machine -> becomes 11:00 in recipient's calendar regardless of zone).
- When DST transitions happen close to the event creation/forwarding time, offsets get confusing (US DST ended this morning), which makes forwarded copies show the wrong absolute time.

What I did:
- Created a new event anchored to Europe/London and exported an explicit .ics that includes TZID and VTIMEZONE blocks.
- Included an explanatory note in the event description and turned off the auto-accept rule for the calendars@quantumretail.com address (suggested).

Attached: quantum-demo-updated.ics (explicit Europe/London TZ). Please use this invite rather than the forwarded one.

Quick checklist for recipients who still see the wrong slot:
- Open the event in Google Calendar and click the three dots -> "Change timezone". Ensure it shows Europe/London.
- If the calendar lists the event as "floating", ask the forwarder to recreate the invite with an explicit TZ.

Sergio — happy for you to send the fixed invite from your mailbox once you're ready.

Thanks,
Karthik
